about.title: Patterson Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Patterson is a small, close-knit city, and when a traffic collision takes a life, the loss ripples through the whole community. Corridors like Sperry Avenue, 2nd Street, Route 33, and Las Palmas Avenue carry steady daily traffic, and while most crashes here result in injury rather than death, the families who face this worst outcome deserve clear answers about what comes next. California law limits who may bring a wrongful death action, generally starting with a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children, and extending to other dependents or heirs when no closer family exists. LawProactive doesn't practice law or represent you directly. Instead, we listen to what happened, then connect you with an independent attorney in our network who can explain your options, evaluate the circumstances of the crash, and help you understand the path toward accountability and support for your family. There's no cost to talk with us, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Families in Patterson Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Can Be Complicated
items.desc: California law prioritizes spouses, domestic partners, and children as the first parties allowed to file, but dependents or other heirs may qualify if no immediate family exists. An independent attorney can help sort out who is legally entitled to bring the claim.

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: Wrongful death claims generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shortens significantly if a government entity, like a public roadway authority, may be responsible. Acting sooner preserves evidence and options.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California allows families to seek funeral and burial costs and lost financial support, along with compensation for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. An attorney can help make sure none of these losses are overlooked.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none of those relatives exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible. An independent attorney can review your family's specific situation to confirm who qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in Patterson?
items.answer: California generally gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. That deadline can be much shorter if a government entity, such as one responsible for road maintenance, may share fault, so it's worth getting guidance early.

items.question: Does a wrongful death claim relate to any criminal charges from the crash?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal case that might arise from the same collision. The two proceedings have different purposes, standards of proof, and timelines, and one does not depend on the outcome of the other.
